chief_data.selection_justification: Selected Candidate 4 as the only viable flow design that meets safety hard gates (BPR > ΔP) and conversion targets (X=0.65). Candidates 2 and 3 were disqualified due to critical BPR violations and insufficient conversion/length constraints. Candidate 4 offers a 3.6x residence time reduction over batch (53 min vs 190 min implied by productivity ratios) with acceptable pressure drop (0.095 bar) and high safety margin.
chief_data.selection_rationale: Candidate 4 is selected as the sole surviving design after Candidates 2 and 3 were disqualified for critical safety (BPR < ΔP) and performance (low conversion/excessive length) failures. Candidate 4 achieves a combined score of 0.765, driven by high safety (0.95) and kinetics (0.85) scores, ensuring stable operation at 120°C in DMF. Candidate 1, while chemically similar, scored lower (0.702) due to poorer fluidics and geometry scores, likely reflecting less optimal mixing or packing efficiency. The user's 'balanced' objective favored Candidate 4's robust safety margin and proven conversion over Candidate 1's marginal gains. The primary remaining uncertainty is the exact mass transfer coefficient in the packed bed, which influences the observed rate constant. The first bench experiment should verify the pressure drop and conversion at the design flow rate to confirm the kinetic model.
